I made apple jelly and I made grape. I decided that since a lot of the recipes I would like to try out require pectin that I wanted to start off trying to make jelly minus the pectin. Maybe that was a mistake, I don't know.

I used apple juice no added calcium (not from concentrate) from the bottle and grape juice (from concentrate) from the store as well. According to the book this was supposed to be just fine.

I followed the recipes exactly and used the thermometer to tell me when I hit the gelling point. I even stuck a few plates in the freezer and ran my finger through the concoction and according to the thermometer and the plates it was destined to be jelly.

Except it's not. I made both Saturday afternoon and stayed up late to finish. I made two batches of apple and two batches of grape. Only one of the jars did not seal properly.

It was more than 12 hours when I popped open my test jars of apple and grape to try and... it wasn't exactly syrup it was more like the consistency of pie filling.

What am I doing wrong???? Could it have been the thermometer or maybe I just haven't let it set up long enough? Also, should I try to re cook it or just dump it and start all over from scratch?

In order for jelly to set properly, you have to strike the correct balance between sugar and pectin. Too little of one and you get syrup. Too much of one and you get something nearing candy in a jar. What's likely happened is that either your pectin is low sugar pectin or the recipe expected you to use low sugar pectin and didn't tell you.

It's possible to save your batch! Try reheating, boiling your batch, add the same amount of sugar again (or double the pectin, someone help me out here) and let it set again. It should be fine.

Edit: wait, you used juice. There's your problem. :) Use frozen fruit (cheaper than fresh)

Not terrible results for the first time canning jelly. What you'll want to do in the future is use pectin- that's going to help you an awful lot. Keep in mind that the more you do it, the better you'll get at it. It's going to get to the point when you don't need a thermometer at all.
